# `provider_reroute`

**Re-route work off an unavailable provider.** Move queued work whose provider is unavailable to the same intelligence class on an available provider, a few tasks at a time; pinned tasks and single-provider classes hold.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Capability | `provider_reroute` |
| Side effect | `composite` |
| Idempotency | natural |
| Retry safe | yes |
| Timeout | none |
| Preview | not supported |

## Purpose

Move queued work off a provider that has run out of usage or lost its login.
When `codex` is unavailable, a `standard-high-codex` task that nobody pinned
should run on `standard-high-claude` instead of waiting out the outage, while
an `astra-high` task (a class only OpenAI serves) and anything a human pinned
to its provider stay where they are with a visible reason. The command does one
sweep of that policy and reports what it moved and what it held
([provider failover](../../specs/provider-failover.md) D11-D16).

## When a playbook uses it

The shipped `provider-failover` system playbook calls it on
`provider.state_changed` and on `timer.5m`. The five-minute tick is what
trickles a dead provider's queue across: a sweep moves at most one pool-width
of work per target rung and at most `reroute.max_per_sweep` tasks, and the next
tick tops up as the moved work is claimed. A project that wants other rules
keeps a project-scope copy of the playbook; the playbook step never forces --
naming tasks, `to_profile` and `force` are operator arguments of
`aq provider reroute`, not of the step.

## How it works internally

1. [`ProviderCommandsMixin._cmd_provider_reroute`](../../../src/commands/provider_commands.py)
   refuses a task-scoped worker token and validates the operator arguments.
2. [`ProviderRerouteService.sweep`](../../../src/providers/reroute.py) gathers
   one snapshot: every worker rung with a class slice for its harness, each
   provider's effective state and generation, the moved-and-queued count per
   rung (`idx_tasks_rerouted`), and the candidates -- READY unassigned tasks on
   an unavailable provider plus automatically-paused ones.
3. The pure planner `plan_sweep` decides per task, in `priority, created_at`
   order: `pinned` holds (`provider_pinned`); a class set to `hold` holds
   (`class_policy_hold`); otherwise it looks for the same class on the next
   provider in `provider_failover.order` (default: the project default's
   provider, then `WORKER_PROVIDERS`), skipping providers the task already
   left, and only an `available` provider is a target. No rung anywhere is
   `no_equivalent_rung`; rungs only on unavailable or degraded providers is
   `no_available_target`; a full trickle is `awaiting_failover_capacity` with
   `ahead`; `reroute.max_auto_per_task` and `task_cooldown_seconds` give
   `reroute_limit_reached`.
4. A provider-paused task (`task_metadata['provider_pause']`) whose provider has
   tripped returns `PAUSED -> READY` first; a pause with no recorded cause is
   touched only with `include_paused`.
5. Each move is one guarded write
   ([`apply_task_reroute`](../../../src/database/queries/task_reroute_queries.py)):
   `profile_id` changes only while the task is queued, unassigned and has no
   live session, in the same transaction as its `task_reroutes` row.

## Side effects and persistence

Per move: `tasks.profile_id`, `tasks.rerouted_from` (the first profile of an
un-undone chain), one `task_reroutes` row (`reason_code =
provider_unavailable`, `batch_id = prb-<provider>-<generation>`), a
system-authored task comment and a `task.rerouted` event. Per batch: one
`provider.reroute_batch` event when it moved or newly held anything, and one
message to `session:supervisor-<project>` per project, keyed by the message
`thread_id` `reroute:<batch>:<project>` so a later sweep of the same outage
never repeats it. Intent and class never change. Everything is durable; a
restart re-plans from the rows.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

| Outcome | Cause | Diagnose with |
|---|---|---|
| `disabled` (success) | `provider_failover.mode` is not `enforce`, or `reroute.enabled` is false; the plan is returned, nothing applied. | `aq system config get provider_failover` |
| `held` (success) | Nothing could move; every held task names its `kind`. | `aq provider reroute --dry-run`, `aq task explain <id>` |
| `rejected` | Re-routing is not running, a worker token called it, or an argument was invalid. | the step's summary; `aq provider status` |

A task a worker claimed between the plan and the write is reported in `lost`
and left alone.

## Example step

```json
{
  "type": "command",
  "rule": "reroute-sweep",
  "title": "reroute",
  "source": {"path": "provider-failover.md", "start_line": 49, "end_line": 55},
  "command": "provider_reroute",
  "inputs": {},
  "save_result_as": "sweep",
  "transitions": {
    "rerouted": "reroute-sweep--done",
    "held": "reroute-sweep--done",
    "idle": "reroute-sweep--done",
    "disabled": "reroute-sweep--done",
    "rejected": "reroute-sweep--failed",
    "runtime_error": "reroute-sweep--failed"
  }
}
```
